title: Reinforcing Agentic Creativity in Scientific Ideation with Night Science
title_zh: Night Science 强化科学构想中的自主创造性

paragraphs.en: Large language models (LLMs) excel at structured, verifiable tasks, but their low-entropy bias can produce homogeneous and predictable outputs, limiting their utility for open-ended scientific ideation. Effective discovery, however, spans a broader creative spectrum: from structured day science to loosely structured, serendipitous night science that reaches ideas beyond those typically considered. We introduce AI Night-Scientist , an agentic framework that uses reinforcement learning to teach models when and how to depart from predictable reasoning. Grounded in cognitive science, we model creativity along three axes: action (what to do and how creatively), process (when to explore versus exploit), and outcome (the novelty and usefulness of the resulting idea). We use these axes to train models with GRPO, exposing them to varying degrees and forms of creativity throughout training. This produces substantially more diverse scientific proposals, expanding the range of research directions by 27.8% and contribution types by 14.9% over the base model. It also improves predicted citation impact by up to 32.0 percentage points and originality by 66.2 points. These gains cannot be reproduced by simply increasing decoding temperature; instead, we find that semantic guidance specifying what kind of creativity to pursue is critical. Overall, our results suggest that creativity is a learnable, multi-level ability that can be shaped to help researchers reach ideas beyond those typically explored by LLMs .

paragraphs.en: Large language models (LLMs) have excelled at structured, systematic tasks with clear verifiability (e.g., coding and quantitative reasoning), where their performance is often improved with reinforcement learning (RL) ( Guo et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2025 ; Zhong and Wang, 2024 ; Liu et al., 2024 ) . This success is consistent with a broader tendency toward minimizing token entropy ( Agarwal et al., 2025 ) , where models favor high-probability outputs that reflect frequent patterns and expected answers in training data ( McCoy et al., 2024 ) . While LLMs have increasingly been applied to scientific ideation ( Si et al., 2025 ; Gottweis et al., 2025 ) , they lack originality ( Zhao et al., 2025 ) , tend to generate homogeneous outputs ( Wenger and Kenett, 2025 ) , and even plagiarize at nontrivial rates ( Gupta and Pruthi, 2025 ) . Ultimately, this directly conflicts with the key attributes of open-ended, creative scientific discovery : novelty, diversity, and serendipity.
paragraphs.zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）在结构清晰、系统性强且易于验证的任务（例如编程和定量推理）中表现出色，而通过强化学习（RL）往往能进一步提升其性能（Guo et al., 2025；Wang et al., 2025；Zhong and Wang, 2024；Liu et al., 2024）。 这一成果与更广泛的降低词元熵的趋势一致（Agarwal et al., 2025），即模型倾向于选择高概率的输出，这些输出反映了训练数据中频繁出现的模式和预期答案（McCoy et al., 2024）。 尽管大型语言模型在科学构想领域的应用日益广泛（Si et al., 2025；Gottweis et al., 2025），但它们缺乏原创性（Zhao et al., 2025），倾向于生成同质化的输出（Wenger and Kenett, 2025），甚至以非微不足道的比例进行抄袭（Gupta and Pruthi, 2025）。 最终，这与开放式、创造性科学发现的关键属性——新颖性、多样性和偶然性——直接冲突。

paragraphs.en: Prior methods depict discovery as a highly structured process, involving hypotheses derived from prior observations and/or data, tested against evidence, and refined or rejected accordingly ( Gottweis et al., 2025 ; Agarwal et al., 2026 ) . But this is only *part* of the scientific discovery process. They typically view creativity as only an attribute of ideas rather than as part of the process, treating individual actions as fixed behaviors (e.g., search, write) and executing them through scaffolded pipelines ( Gu et al., 2024 ; Lu et al., 2024 ) . While this supports the critical reasoning crucial for validating existing ideas, this overlooks the creative reasoning necessary for discovering new ones. Both are complementary and crucial perspectives of scientific discovery, referred to as day and night science ( Wechsler et al., 2018 ; Halpern, 2007 ; Stent, 1988 ; Yanai and Lercher, 2019 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 以往的方法将发现描述为一个高度结构化的过程，其中包括基于先前观察和/或数据得出的假设，这些假设会与证据进行检验，并据此得到改进或否定（Gottweis 等人，2025；Agarwal 等人，2026）。 但这只是科学发现过程的*一部分*。 他们通常认为创造力仅仅是想法的一种属性，而非过程的一部分，并将个体行为视为固定的行动（例如搜索、写作），并通过结构化的流程来执行这些行为（Gu 等人，2024；Lu 等人，2024）。 虽然这种方法支持了验证现有想法所必需的关键推理，但却忽视了发现新想法所需的创造性推理。 这两种视角是科学发现中相互补充且至关重要的，被称为“白昼与黑夜科学”（Wechsler 等人，2018；Halpern，2007；Stent，1988；Yanai 和 Lercher，2019）。

paragraphs.en: Night science captures the often-neglected nature of human-driven discovery: loosely structured and dynamic exploration driven by highly creative actions, such as exploring distant analogies (e.g., biology-inspired technology), considering alternative perspectives after serendipitous encounters (e.g., debates with colleagues from other domains), and acting on partly-formalized intuitions (e.g., abandoning status quo assumptions). Together, day and night science form a spectrum that human researchers have smoothly traversed to uncover breakthroughs ( de Chantal and Markovits, 2022 ; Dwyer et al., 2025 ) , such as chemotherapy and penicillin ( Hirsch, 2006 ; Ligon, 2004 ) .

paragraphs.en: Action-level ( how ): Associates each action with a creativity level, allowing the same action to vary from conventional, high-probability behavior to more exploratory and unconventional behavior.
paragraphs.zh: 行动层面（方式）：将每个行动与一个创造力水平相关联，使得同一行动可以从常规、高概率的行为转变为更具探索性和非传统性的行为。

paragraphs.en: Scientific discovery has been characterized as an interplay between structured, hypothesis-driven day science and more exploratory, intuition- and serendipity-driven night science ( Stent, 1988 ; Yanai and Lercher, 2019 ) . Classic theories of creativity characterize creative thought through remote associations between otherwise distant concepts ( Mednick, 1962 ) , generative and exploratory modes of cognition ( Ward et al., 1999 ) , and outcomes that are both original and useful ( Runco and Jaeger, 2012 ) . Creativity can also vary in degree: prior work describes a continuum of creative behavior ( Cohen, 1989 ) , with problem-solving strategies ranging from paradigm-preserving to paradigm-stretching and paradigm-breaking ( McFadzean, 1998 ) . Related accounts distinguish between exploring existing conceptual spaces and transforming them to enable qualitatively new ideas ( Boden, 1998 ) , while theories of creative ideation show that originality can arise either by flexibly exploring many conceptual directions or by persistently exploring a few in greater depth ( Nijstad et al., 2010 ) . Together, these perspectives motivate our view of creativity as varying both where it enters reasoning (within actions, processes, and outcomes) and how strongly it is expressed.
paragraphs.zh: 科学发现的特点在于结构化、以假说为导向的“日间科学”与更具探索性、依赖直觉和偶然发现的“夜间科学”之间的相互作用（Stent，1988；Yanai 和 Lercher，2019）。 经典的创造力理论通过原本遥远概念之间的远程联想（Mednick，1962）、生成性与探索性的认知模式（Ward 等，1999），以及兼具原创性和实用性的成果（Runco 和 Jaeger，2012）来描述创造性思维。 创造力的程度也存在差异：先前的研究将创造性行为描述为一个连续体（Cohen，1989），其问题解决策略从维持范式、拓展范式到突破范式不等（McFadzean，1998）。 相关理论区分了探索现有概念空间与将其转化为支持全新想法的方式（Boden，1998）；而创造性构想理论则表明，原创性既可以通过灵活探索多种概念方向产生，也可以通过持续深入探索少数方向实现（Nijstad 等，2010）。 综合来看，这些观点促使我们将创造力视为在推理过程中介入的位置（包括行为、过程和成果）及其表达强度上存在差异的概念。

paragraphs.en: This view contrasts with most current LLM-based approaches to scientific discovery. Existing research agents broaden ideation through retrieval, search, multi-agent interaction, and iterative generation ( Gu et al., 2024 ; Lu et al., 2024 ; Kargupta et al., 2025a ; Gottweis et al., 2025 ) , but generally treat actions such as searching, debating, and writing as fixed behaviors and primarily assess creativity in the resulting idea. This leaves little control over how creatively individual actions are performed or when creative deviations should occur throughout reasoning. Relatedly, Kargupta et al. (2025b) find that LLMs struggle with the metacognitive awareness needed to monitor and adapt their reasoning, further limiting their ability to flexibly shift between critical and creative modes.
paragraphs.zh: 这种观点与大多数当前基于大型语言模型（LLM）的科学发现方法形成对比。 现有的研究智能体通过检索、搜索、多智能体交互和迭代生成来拓展创意（Gu et al., 2024; Lu et al., 2024; Kargupta et al., 2025a; Gottweis et al., 2025），但通常将搜索、辩论和写作等行为视为固定模式，并主要根据最终产生的创意来评估创造力。 这使得个体行为如何富有创意地执行，以及在推理过程中何时应出现创造性偏离，几乎无法被控制。 与此相关，Kargupta et al. (2025b) 发现，大型语言模型难以具备监控和调整自身推理所需的元认知意识，这进一步限制了它们在批判性与创造性模式之间灵活切换的能力。

paragraphs.en: Recent work has begun targeting the mechanisms that produce creative scientific ideas. O’Neill et al. (2025) use structured assumption inversion to generate novel hypotheses, inspiring the spark action in our framework, while Kargupta et al. (2025c) and Kargupta et al. (2026) use retrieval to identify research gaps and surface interdisciplinary inspiration. Other work instead learns scientific capabilities directly: GIANTS ( He-Yueya et al., 2026 ) trains smaller models to anticipate scientific insights, while Tong et al. (2026) study whether models can learn scientific taste. Together, these approaches suggest that not only scientific outputs, but also the processes that produce them, can be shaped through structure and supervision. Reinforcement learning offers a way to shape this process without prescribing exactly how discovery should unfold, although open-ended ideation has no single correct answer and must balance qualities such as novelty, relevance, feasibility, and usefulness ( Afzal et al., 2025 ) . Moreover, useful creative exploration requires more than simply injecting randomness ( Schmidhuber, 2010 ) . Our work builds on these ideas by learning both how creatively individual actions should be performed and when different levels of creativity are useful across a reasoning trajectory.
paragraphs.zh: 近期的研究开始关注那些能够产生创造性科学思想的机制。O’Neill等人（2025）利用结构化的假设反转方法生成新颖的假说，这启发我们在框架中引入了“火花”这一操作；而Kargupta等人（2025c）和Kargupta等人（2026）则通过信息检索来识别研究空白，并挖掘跨学科灵感。其他研究则选择直接学习科学能力：GIANTS（He-Yueya等人，2026）训练较小的模型以预测科学洞见，而Tong等人（2026）则探讨了模型是否能够学会科学的“品味”。综合来看，这些方法表明，不仅科学产出本身，甚至产生这些产出的过程，也可以通过结构和监督加以塑造。强化学习提供了一种塑造这一过程的方式，而无需预先规定发现过程必须如何展开——尽管开放式创意生成没有唯一正确答案，必须在新颖性、相关性、可行性和实用性等特性之间取得平衡（Afzal等人，2025）。此外，富有成效的创造性探索不仅需要简单地注入随机性（Schmidhuber，2010）。我们的研究在此基础上进一步探索：既学习个体行动应如何以创造性的方式执行，也学习在推理过程中不同阶段的创造力水平何时最为有效。

paragraphs.en: We propose AI Night-Scientist , as illustrated in Figure 2 , which represents creativity directly within the agent’s reasoning trajectory rather than only in its final output. We extend the ReAct-style reasoning setting ( Yao et al., 2023 ) : at each step, the agent selects an action together with a creativity level that specifies how that action should be carried out, executes it, and updates its current idea state. Repeating this process produces a trajectory through the space of possible ideas, allowing the agent to move between more familiar and more unexplored directions as reasoning unfolds. This lets us represent creativity at three levels (Figure 1 ): action-level creativity captures how an action is performed, process-level creativity captures when to shift between lower- and higher-creativity actions, and outcome-level creativity captures the novelty and usefulness of the resulting idea.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 AI Night-Scientist（如圖 2 所示），它將創造性直接表示在智能體的推理軌跡中，而不仅仅是最終輸出中。 我們擴展了 ReAct 風格的推理設定（Yao et al., 2023）：在每一步中，智能體會選擇一個行動，同時指定一個創造性水平來說明該行動應如何執行，然後執行該行動並更新其当前的想法狀態。 重複此過程會產生一條穿越可能想法空間的軌跡，使智能體在推理過程中能夠在較為熟悉和較為未探索的方向之間轉換。 這讓我們能夠在三層面上表示創造性（圖 1）：行動層面的創造性描述了行動的執行方式，過程層面的創造性描述了在低創造性和高創造性行動之間切換的時機，而結果層面的創造性則描述了最終想法的新穎性和實用性。

paragraphs.en: Together, this multi-level representation separates how creativity is expressed within an action, when different degrees of creativity are useful across reasoning, and what the process ultimately produces. We represent action-level creativity in natural language to make these choices interpretable and give the user direct semantic control over how and to what extent each action may deviate from its conventional execution. The number and meaning of creativity levels can also vary by action.

paragraphs.en: We focus on proposals with a scope similar to long-term research grants, where ideas are intended to guide work over several years rather than describe an immediately executable experiment. The task therefore rewards reasoning that can move beyond established directions while still producing ideas that are feasible and relevant to p p .
paragraphs.zh: 我们重点关注范围与长期研究资助类似的提案，这些提案旨在为持续数年的工作提供指导，而非描述一个可以立即执行的实验。 这使得该场景非常适合研究创造性推理：提案必须基于现有研究，但其许多核心观点在推理阶段无法直接验证，因为所需的实验或数据可能尚未存在。 因此，这项任务会奖励那些能够超越既有方向，同时仍能提出可行且与 p p 相关的观点的推理能力。

paragraphs.en: To teach models when and how different degrees of creativity are useful, we leverage reinforcement learning. RL allows the quality of the final idea to shape the reasoning process without prescribing how that process should unfold. Our training pipeline consists of two phases: (i) a rollout phase , where the agent constructs a reasoning trajectory τ \tau using the creativity-aligned action space above, and (ii) a reward phase , where the resulting proposal o o is evaluated. We use Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) ( Shao et al., 2024 ) , which learns from relative rewards across sampled trajectories without requiring a separate critic. In our primary setting, the reward is applied only to the final proposal, requiring the model to learn which actions to take, how creatively to perform them, and how to sequence them based on their eventual effect on proposal quality.
paragraphs.zh: 为了教会模型何时以及如何运用不同程度的创造力，我们借助强化学习。 强化学习能让最终想法的质量反过来塑造推理过程，而无需预先规定该过程的具体展开方式。 我们的训练流程包含两个阶段：（i）展开阶段，智能体利用上述与创造力对齐的动作空间构建一条推理轨迹 τ；（ii）奖励阶段，对由此产生的提案 o 进行评估。 我们采用群体相对策略优化（GRPO）（Shao 等人，2024），该方法通过采样轨迹间的相对奖励进行学习，无需额外的评判模型。 在我们的主要设置中，奖励仅作用于最终提案，这要求模型学会采取哪些行动、以何种创造性的方式执行这些行动，以及如何根据它们对提案质量的最终影响来安排行动顺序。

paragraphs.en: Scientific proposals contain multiple ideas whose novelty and feasibility may differ substantially, making a single holistic quality judgment difficult to ground. We therefore first decompose the final proposal into its atomic research ideas, separating what each phase proposes from how it plans to execute it. We then evaluate each component against the original research problem and relevant literature along three dimensions: precedence , feasibility , and relevance (Table 2 ).

paragraphs.en: Outcome-only training still leaves the model to discover useful creative behaviors through their eventual effect on proposal quality. We therefore explore two additional forms of guidance: exposing the model to occasional serendipitous actions early in training, and directly rewarding properties of the intermediate reasoning process. paragraphs.en: We construct our dataset from the NSF Awards Database 2 2 2 https://huggingface.co/datasets/davidheineman/nsf-awards , focusing on Computer Science, Engineering, and Mathematics (CSE) awards from 2018 onward. We use a 90 : 10 90{:}10 train/test split, yielding 4,414 training and 491 test awards. Our model receives only the award title as p p , which typically describes a broad, long-horizon research problem; we withhold the award abstract, project outcomes, and associated publications so that generation is not anchored to the funded solution. We focus on CSE to ensure broad coverage in open-access arXiv literature, while retaining substantial interdisciplinary breadth: the training set spans 46 research domains, with 23.1% of subfield labels in core AI/ML and over 48% of label occurrences outside AI/ML and core CS and Engineering (Appendix B ).

paragraphs.en: Original NSF grant proposals are not publicly available, so we construct reconstructed reference proposals from evidence surrounding each funded project. For each award, we collect its abstract, project outcomes report, PI information, and award period, then retrieve likely associated arXiv papers by the award PIs. Candidate papers are ranked using PI overlap, topical similarity, publication timing, and explicit funding acknowledgments. We prompt GPT-5.1 to treat these sources as downstream evidence and reconstruct a plausible pre-award research plan that could have led to the observed project and publications. The reference follows the same structured format as generated proposals, including a summary, background, and multi-phase research plan.
paragraphs.zh: 原始的国家科学基金会（NSF）资助提案并非公开可用，因此我们根据每个已获资助项目的相关证据构建重构的参考提案。 对于每项资助，我们会收集其摘要、项目成果报告、首席研究员（PI）信息以及资助周期，然后检索由这些首席研究员发表的、可能相关的 arXiv 论文。 候选论文将根据首席研究员的重合度、主题相似性、发表时间以及明确的资金致谢进行排序。 我们提示 GPT-5.1 将这些资料视为下游证据，重构一个在资助前可能促成所观察到的项目和研究成果的合理研究计划。 该参考提案采用与生成提案相同的结构化格式，包括摘要、背景以及多阶段研究计划。

Rather, they provide standardized, evidence-grounded references for research directions that were actually funded and subsequently pursued. We use them only as matched references for pairwise evaluation, and the proposal-generating model never receives the oracle information used to construct them. paragraphs.en: Scientific creativity is difficult to capture with any single automatic metric, particularly because the long-term value of a research idea may not be observable for years. We therefore evaluate models along three complementary dimensions: predicted citation impact , literature-grounded originality , and research idea diversity . Together, these capture both the quality of individual proposals and the range of research directions explored across the dataset.
paragraphs.zh: 科学创造力很难用任何单一的自动指标来衡量，尤其是因为一个研究想法的长期价值可能需要多年才能显现。 因此，我们从三个相互补充的维度来评估模型：预测的引用影响力、基于文献的原创性以及研究想法的多样性。 这些维度共同捕捉了单个提案的质量以及数据集中所探索的研究方向的广度。

paragraphs.en: Predicted Citation Impact. For each problem, we compare the generated proposal against its matched reconstructed reference in randomized order and report pairwise win rate. We use SciJudge ( Tong et al., 2026 ) , a 30B-parameter model trained to predict relative citation impact from large-scale community signals, as a proxy for the potential usefulness and downstream value of the proposed research (prompts in Appendix G ). It has an average 82.7 % 82.7\% citation prediction accuracy.

paragraphs.en: Research Idea Diversity. Pairwise metrics capture the quality of individual proposals but not whether a model repeatedly produces the same kinds of ideas. Following the annotation format of Chen et al. (2026) , we use GPT-5.4-mini to classify each proposal by its primary research idea paradigm and, analogously, by its primary contribution type using categories adapted from prior taxonomies ( Wobbrock, 2012 ; Miles, 2017 ) . For each taxonomy, we report the effective number of categories represented (Appendix H ), normalized by the seven available categories; higher values indicate a broader and more balanced range of research directions. The research-paradigm judge Chen et al. (2026) achieves κ = 0.84 \kappa=0.84 agreement with human judgments on 150 samples.
paragraphs.zh: 研究思路多样性。成对度量指标能够捕捉单个提案的质量，但无法判断模型是否反复生成相同类型的研究思路。遵循 Chen et al. (2026) 的标注格式，我们使用 GPT-5.4-mini 根据每个提案的主要研究思路范式对其进行分类，并类似地根据其主要贡献类型进行分类，所用类别改编自先前的分类体系（Wobbrock, 2012；Miles, 2017）。对于每种分类体系，我们报告其实际代表的类别数量（附录 H），并以可用的七个类别进行归一化处理；数值越高，表明研究方向的覆盖范围越广且越均衡。在 150 个样本上，研究范式评判者 Chen et al. (2026) 与人类判断的一致性系数 κ = 0.84 \kappa=0.84。

paragraphs.en: Table 3 (a) shows a consistent advantage for AI Night-Scientist over both direct-generation and agentic baselines. In comparison, scaling the zero-shot model from 8B to 14B yields almost no improvement, whereas scaling AI Night-Scientist adds another 3.29 points in citation and 12.36 points in originality. Additional model capacity therefore appears substantially more useful once paired with a learned creative reasoning policy.

paragraphs.en: The contrast with temperature-based exploration is especially evident after RL. Although both optimize the same proposal-level reward, Night-8B exceeds the temperature-controlled variant by 36.50 points in originality and 18.37 points in citation. ReAct closes much of this gap, showing that a learned multi-step policy already helps, but semantic creativity levels still add 9.72 points in originality and 4.95 points in citation. The useful signal is therefore not simply to “explore more,” but to specify how an action should deviate so RL can learn when those deviations are useful.
paragraphs.zh: 与基于温度的探索方法相比，这种差异在强化学习（RL）之后尤为明显。 尽管两者都在优化相同的提案级奖励，但在原创性方面，Night-8B 比温度控制版本高出 36.50 分，在引用方面高出 18.37 分。 ReAct 大幅缩小了这一差距，表明已学习的多步策略已经有所帮助，但语义创造力仍能为原创性增加 9.72 分，为引用增加 4.95 分。 因此，有效的信号并非简单地“更多探索”，而是明确说明动作应如何偏离，以便强化学习能够学会在何种情况下这些偏离是有益的。

paragraphs.en: We examine one representative NSF topic to understand how proposal directions differ qualitatively across methods. paragraphs.en: We introduce AI Night-Scientist , a creativity-aligned agentic framework that represents creativity at the action, process, and outcome levels and uses reinforcement learning to teach models when and how to depart from predictable reasoning. Applied to long-horizon research proposal generation, AI Night-Scientist improves predicted citation impact and originality by up to 32.03 and 66.15 points over its base model, while producing a broader range of research paradigms. These gains are not reproduced by higher decoding temperature or ReAct alone, supporting our central finding that creativity is more than sampling stochasticity. Our ablations further show that outcome-only training provides the strongest overall balance of quality and diversity, while process-level rewards can increase originality at the cost of citation impact and breadth. Together, these results suggest that creativity can be learned as a multi-level reasoning capability, enabling scientific agents to move more flexibly between the structured reasoning of day science and the exploratory reasoning of night science while remaining tools for human-led discovery.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 AI Night-Scientist，一个与创造力相契合的智能体框架。该框架在行为、过程和结果三个层面体现创造力，并利用强化学习来教导模型何时以及如何偏离可预测的推理方式。 在长期研究提案生成任务中，AI Night-Scientist 相较于其基础模型，将预测的引用影响和原创性分别提升了最多 32.03 和 66.15 分，同时生成了更广泛的研究范式。 仅通过提高解码温度或使用 ReAct 方法无法复现这些提升，这支持了我们的核心发现：创造力不仅仅是随机采样的结果。 我们的消融研究进一步表明，仅针对结果的训练在质量与多样性之间实现了最佳平衡；而过程层面的奖励虽然能提升原创性，但会牺牲引用影响和广度。 综合来看，这些结果表明创造力可以作为一种多层级推理能力被学习，使科学智能体能够在日间的结构化推理与夜间的探索性推理之间更灵活地切换，同时仍作为人类主导的发现工具。

paragraphs.en: AI Night-Scientist is designed for early-stage scientific ideation, when research directions are still speculative and not yet fully testable. Its role is to help researchers explore a broader set of possible directions, including connections or assumptions they may not otherwise consider. The system is intended as a creative collaborator rather than an autonomous researcher: generated proposals should be treated as candidate ideas that require critical evaluation, refinement, and validation by domain experts before they can support scientific conclusions.
paragraphs.zh: AI 夜间科学家专为早期科学构想而设计，此时研究方向仍处于推测阶段，尚无法完全验证。 它的作用在于帮助研究人员探索更广泛的可能方向，包括他们原本可能不会考虑到的关联或假设。 该系统旨在成为一位富有创意的协作伙伴，而非一个自主的研究人员：所生成的提案应被视为候选构想，在能够支持科学结论之前，需要由领域专家进行批判性评估、完善和验证。

paragraphs.en: Human ideation is often shaped by the concepts and examples already available in their local research community ( Lubart, 2001 ) . By encouraging proposals that depart from existing work while remaining relevant and feasible, AI Night-Scientist aims to surface directions beyond those most immediately accessible to a researcher or model. This may be especially useful for interdisciplinary exploration, where relevant ideas can be distributed across distant literature and research communities. Importantly, broader exploration does not imply that unfamiliar ideas are inherently better; their scientific value must still be established through expert judgment and empirical validation.
paragraphs.zh: 人类的构想往往受到其本地研究社群中已有概念和范例的影响（Lubart，2001）。 AI Night-Scientist 鼓励提出既偏离现有成果、又保持相关性和可行性的方案，旨在发掘研究人员或模型无法直接触及的研究方向。 这种方法在跨学科探索中可能尤其有用，因为相关的想法可能分散在遥远的文献和研究社群中。 重要的是，更广泛的探索并不意味着不熟悉的想法本质上更好；其科学价值仍需通过专家判断和实证验证来确立。

paragraphs.en: As with other generative systems for scientific writing, AI Night-Scientist can produce plausible but incorrect, infeasible, or insufficiently grounded proposals, and could be misused to generate low-quality scientific content at scale. Its outputs should therefore be presented as AI-generated suggestions rather than validated research plans. Responsible use requires transparent disclosure, independent verification of claims and citations, and meaningful human oversight before ideas are pursued, disseminated, or incorporated into scientific work.

paragraphs.en: We select NSF CSE awards from 2018 onwards. Non-research grants (e.g., travel and conference grants) are excluded. paragraphs.en: To characterize the topical breadth of the training set, we applied an automated three-stage taxonomy pipeline to the 4,414 NSF award titles. paragraphs.en: We report per-domain win rates for AI Night-Scientist-8B and Qwen3-8B zero-shot against the reference proposals across 36 canonical research domains (Table 7 ). paragraphs.en: We qualitatively compare proposals on the NSF topic “Using Artificial Intelligence to Transform Online Video Lectures into Effective and Inclusive Agent-Based Presentations.” GPT-4.1 produces a well-structured but generic proposal that restates existing approaches (e.g., lecture segmentation and conversational agents) without introducing a distinguishing mechanism. ReAct adds a concrete multimodal engagement score but leaves its reinforcement learning formulation underspecified. AI Night-Scientist-8B (outcome-only) introduces the novel Agentify concept—treating lectures as live, co-created sessions in which an AI agent interleaves questions and dialogues in real time, rather than optimizing pre-recorded content after the fact. The process-reward variant proposes Progressive Content Enactors (PCEs), which deliberately introduce controlled errors and ambiguities into lectures to force students to actively resolve them (analogous to how working through a flawed proof teaches more than reading a perfect one), though its background section overreaches with unverifiable metrics. Table 8 provides excerpts and error analysis; key novel or well-specified contributions are highlighted in green , while vague, incremental, or questionable claims are highlighted in red .

paragraphs.en: Each action in the AI Night-Scientist framework is realized through a structured LLM prompt that takes the current problem p p , creativity level c c , and the accumulated trajectory context as inputs, and returns a JSON output. paragraphs.en: The search action generates up to five arXiv search queries. Retrieved papers are parsed and appended to the trajectory context for use by subsequent actions.

paragraphs.en: The debate action is executed in two sequential steps: (i) generating a debate setup (participants, topics, and structure) and (ii) simulating the debate conversation. The creativity level controls participant diversity and discussion structure, ranging from a focused single-turn discussion with a same-field colleague (level 1) to an open-ended, multi-turn panel with cross-disciplinary experts (level 5). The conversation is appended verbatim to the trajectory context.
paragraphs.zh: 辩论操作分两个顺序步骤执行：(i) 生成辩论设置（参与者、主题和结构），以及 (ii) 模拟辩论对话。 创造力水平控制参与者的多样性和讨论结构，范围从与同领域同事进行的聚焦性单轮讨论（第 1 级）到跨学科专家参与的开放式多轮小组讨论（第 5 级）。 对话将逐字添加到轨迹上下文中。

paragraphs.en: The spark action generates a “Bit-Flip” idea ( O’Neill et al., 2025 ) : it inverts a commonly held assumption to produce a novel research direction. The creativity level governs the scope of the challenged assumption, from a specific proposal-level constraint (level 1) to a field-reshaping paradigm shift (level 5). The Bit-Flip is appended to the trajectory context and can influence subsequent write and action-selection steps.
paragraphs.zh: “火花”操作会生成一个“比特翻转”的创意（O’Neill 等，2025）：它通过反转一个普遍接受的假设，从而开辟一个新的研究方向。 创造力水平决定了被挑战假设的范围，从具体的提案级限制（第 1 级）到能够重塑整个领域的范式转变（第 5 级）。 “比特翻转”会被附加到轨迹上下文中，并可能影响后续的写入和智能体选择步骤。

paragraphs.en: We classify each proposal by its primary scholarly contribution using GPT-5.4-mini and a seven-way taxonomy adapted from Wobbrock (2012) . The contribution types are: empirical , which produces new findings from systematically gathered or analyzed data; artifact , which creates a novel instantiated system, tool, process, intervention, or other constructed artifact; methodological , which introduces or refines a reusable method; theoretical , which develops reusable concepts, models, principles, hypotheses, or frameworks; benchmark or dataset , which contributes a reusable data or evaluation resource; survey , which synthesizes existing work into higher-level understanding; and opinion , which advances an evidence-grounded position intended to persuade or redirect discussion.
paragraphs.zh: 我们使用 GPT-5.4-mini 和改编自 Wobbrock (2012) 的七分类法，根据每项提案的主要学术贡献对其进行分类。 贡献类型包括：实证类（empirical），即通过系统收集或分析数据产生新发现；成果类（artifact），即创建一种新颖的具体系统、工具、流程、干预措施或其他构建的成果；方法论类（methodological），即引入或改进可复用的方法；理论类（theoretical），即发展可复用的概念、模型、原则、假设或框架；基准或数据集类（benchmark or dataset），即贡献可复用的数据或评估资源；综述类（survey），即将现有研究综合起来形成更高层次的理解；以及观点类（opinion），即提出基于证据的立场，旨在说服他人或引导讨论方向。

paragraphs.en: Distinction from research-idea paradigms. Contribution type captures what form of scholarly output the proposal ultimately contributes, whereas the research-idea paradigm captures what high-level research move is used to turn an opportunity into a proposed direction. Following the research-idea annotation setup of Chen et al. (2026) , our paradigm categories distinguish moves such as assumption relaxation, failure mitigation, formal derivation, empirical mapping, artifact construction, and optimization. The two axes are therefore complementary rather than redundant. For example, an artifact contribution may arise from relaxing an assumption, mitigating a failure, or optimizing resource use; conversely, a measurement-oriented research idea may ultimately contribute either empirical findings or a reusable benchmark.
paragraphs.zh: 与研究构想范式的区别。贡献类型体现了该提案最终产生的学术成果形式，而研究构想范式则体现了将机会转化为所提方向时采用的高层次研究策略。遵循 Chen 等人（2026）提出的研究构想标注框架，我们的范式类别区分了诸如假设放宽、失败缓解、形式化推导、经验性映射、产物构建和优化等策略。因此，这两个维度是互补的，而非冗余的。例如，一项产物类贡献可能源于对假设的放宽、对失败的缓解或资源使用的优化；反之，一项以测量为导向的研究构想最终可能产生经验性发现或可复用的基准。

paragraphs.en: Primary-label selection. The classifier is instructed to distinguish the proposal’s central contribution from methods or artifacts that merely support it. In particular, empirical contributions are defined by the new findings produced from data, while benchmark or dataset contributions are defined by the reusable resource itself. Similarly, artifact contributions center on a novel instantiated invention, whereas methodological contributions center on a reusable way of conducting research or practice. Theoretical contributions may be empirically evaluated, but the reusable concept, explanation, model, or framework must remain the principal contribution.
paragraphs.zh: 主标签的选择。 分类器被要求区分提案的核心贡献与仅用于支持该提案的方法或成果。 具体而言，经验性贡献由从数据中产生的新发现定义，而基准或数据集贡献则由可重用的资源本身定义。 类似地，成果贡献聚焦于一个新颖的具体实现发明，而方法论贡献则聚焦于一种可重复使用的研究或实践方式。 理论性贡献可以经过经验验证，但可重用的概念、解释、模型或框架必须仍然是主要贡献。

paragraphs.en: We assess Originality using GPT-5.1 as a judge in a pairwise setting. For each test instance, the model-generated proposal and the matched reconstructed reference proposal are each submitted to our arXiv retrieval system; the top-1 closest paper is retrieved for each using sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedding-based search. The retrieval query is constructed from the proposal title concatenated with the first three sentences of the proposal summary. Proposal order (A vs. B) is randomized per-pair using a deterministic seed to eliminate position bias.

paragraphs.en: The judge is instructed to assess originality relative to both the competing proposal and the closest retrieved paper for each proposal. This prevents superficially creative proposals from scoring well if their core idea closely mirrors existing literature. The judgment emphasizes: (i) originality of the central concept, (ii) distance from the retrieved nearest neighbor, (iii) whether the proposal recombines familiar ideas or opens a genuinely new technical direction, and (iv) depth of novelty over breadth or terminological density.

paragraphs.en: To assess the reliability of our automated evaluation metrics, we conducted a small-scale human evaluation in which two expert annotators independently judged 33 pairwise proposal comparisons (covering all three model variants: Qwen3-8B-Base, GPT-4.1, and AI Night-Scientist-8B). paragraphs.en: Original NSF grant proposals are not publicly available. We therefore construct reconstructed reference proposals from evidence surrounding each funded project. These reconstructions are not intended to reproduce the original proposal text; rather, they provide standardized, evidence-grounded references for research directions that were actually funded and subsequently pursued. The proposal-generating model never receives the award abstracts, project outcomes, or associated publications used in this reconstruction.
paragraphs.zh: 原始的NSF资助提案并不公开可用。 因此，我们从每个已获资助项目的相关证据中构建重构的参考提案。 这些重构并非旨在重现原始提案文本；相反，它们为实际获得资助并随后开展的研究方向提供了标准化、基于证据的参考。 提案生成模型从未接收过用于此次重构的获奖摘要、项目成果或相关出版物。

sents.zh: 原始的NSF资助提案并不公开可用。

sents.en: We therefore construct reconstructed reference proposals from evidence surrounding each funded project.
sents.zh: 因此，我们从每个已获资助项目的相关证据中构建重构的参考提案。

sents.en: The proposal-generating model never receives the award abstracts, project outcomes, or associated publications used in this reconstruction.
sents.zh: 提案生成模型从未接收过用于此次重构的获奖摘要、项目成果或相关出版物。

paragraphs.en: Collect award evidence. For each award, we collect its title, abstract, project outcomes report (POR), PI names, award ID, and award period from the NSF Awards Database.
paragraphs.zh: 收集奖项证据。 对于每个奖项，我们从美国国家科学基金会（NSF）奖项数据库中收集其名称、摘要、项目成果报告（POR）、首席研究员姓名、奖项编号和奖项周期。

sents.en: Collect award evidence.
sents.zh: 收集奖项证据。

sents.en: For each award, we collect its title, abstract, project outcomes report (POR), PI names, award ID, and award period from the NSF Awards Database.
sents.zh: 对于每个奖项，我们从美国国家科学基金会（NSF）奖项数据库中收集其名称、摘要、项目成果报告（POR）、首席研究员姓名、奖项编号和奖项周期。

paragraphs.en: Retrieve likely associated papers by PI. We use PI-first retrieval over arXiv, issuing up to 12 author-based queries using PI full names, surnames, and combinations of multiple PIs. Results are deduplicated by arXiv ID. This constrains retrieval to papers plausibly authored by the funded investigators before using topical information to determine which papers are most closely associated with the award.
paragraphs.zh: 根据首席研究员（PI）检索可能相关的论文。 我们优先使用首席研究员（PI）信息进行 arXiv 检索，最多发出 12 次基于作者的查询，使用 PI 的全名、姓氏以及多位 PI 的组合信息。 通过 arXiv ID 对结果进行去重处理。 此举将检索范围限制在可能由受资助的研究人员撰写且早于该奖项的论文，随后再利用主题信息确定哪些论文与奖项最为相关。

sents.en: Retrieve likely associated papers by PI.
sents.zh: 根据首席研究员（PI）检索可能相关的论文。

sents.en: We use PI-first retrieval over arXiv, issuing up to 12 author-based queries using PI full names, surnames, and combinations of multiple PIs.
sents.zh: 我们优先使用首席研究员（PI）信息进行 arXiv 检索，最多发出 12 次基于作者的查询，使用 PI 的全名、姓氏以及多位 PI 的组合信息。

sents.en: Results are deduplicated by arXiv ID.
sents.zh: 通过 arXiv ID 对结果进行去重处理。

paragraphs.en: Rank candidate papers using award evidence. Candidate papers are first ranked using PI-author overlap, topical overlap between the award evidence (title, abstract, and POR) and the paper title and abstract, and publication timing relative to the award period. We additionally reward cases in which the award title appears directly in the paper abstract. PI overlap receives the strongest weight so that topical similarity alone cannot make an unrelated paper a strong candidate.
paragraphs.zh: 根据获奖证据对候选论文进行排序。 候选论文首先基于以下因素进行排序：PI与作者的重叠度、获奖证据（标题、摘要和POR）与论文标题及摘要之间的主题重叠度，以及与获奖时间段的发表时间关系。 此外，如果获奖标题直接出现在论文摘要中，我们还会给予额外奖励。 PI重叠度的权重最高，因此仅凭主题相似性无法使一篇无关的论文成为强有力的候选者。

sents.en: Rank candidate papers using award evidence.
sents.zh: 根据获奖证据对候选论文进行排序。

sents.en: Candidate papers are first ranked using PI-author overlap, topical overlap between the award evidence (title, abstract, and POR) and the paper title and abstract, and publication timing relative to the award period.
sents.zh: 候选论文首先基于以下因素进行排序：PI与作者的重叠度、获奖证据（标题、摘要和POR）与论文标题及摘要之间的主题重叠度，以及与获奖时间段的发表时间关系。

sents.zh: 此外，如果获奖标题直接出现在论文摘要中，我们还会给予额外奖励。

sents.zh: PI重叠度的权重最高，因此仅凭主题相似性无法使一篇无关的论文成为强有力的候选者。

paragraphs.en: Verify candidates using full-text evidence. For the highest-ranked candidates, we retrieve the paper text and extract the abstract, introduction, methods or approach, and experiments or results, excluding references and appendices where possible. We then rescore papers using full-text evidence, including explicit mention of the NSF award ID, NSF funding acknowledgments, PI surnames, and topical overlap with the award. We retain up to three highly ranked papers per award. If no paper passes the grounding threshold, we retain the strongest PI-matched papers with usable text so that reconstruction remains grounded in likely investigator-authored work.
paragraphs.zh: 使用全文证据验证候选论文。 对于排名最高的候选论文，我们检索其全文文本，并提取摘要、引言、方法或研究方案以及实验或结果部分，在可能的情况下排除参考文献和附录。 接着，我们利用全文证据对论文重新评分，包括明确提及的 NSF 奖项 ID、NSF 资助致谢、首席研究员（PI）的姓氏以及与该奖项相关的主题重叠度。 每个奖项最多保留三篇排名靠前的论文。 如果没有论文通过基准验证阈值，我们将保留与首席研究员匹配度最高且文本可用的论文，以确保重建结果仍基于研究者本人可能撰写的工作。

sents.zh: 使用全文证据验证候选论文。

sents.zh: 每个奖项最多保留三篇排名靠前的论文。

sents.zh: 如果没有论文通过基准验证阈值，我们将保留与首席研究员匹配度最高且文本可用的论文，以确保重建结果仍基于研究者本人可能撰写的工作。

paragraphs.en: Reconstruct a plausible pre-award research plan. We prompt GPT-5.1 as an expert NSF PI using the award metadata, POR, and selected papers. Crucially, the prompt treats publications as downstream evidence of what the funded project ultimately produced and asks the model to infer a plausible pre-award research plan that could have led to those outcomes, rather than summarize or copy the papers. The model is instructed not to mention the reconstruction process and to produce the same structured format used by our generated proposals: a proposal summary, background and significance, and a multi-phase research plan specifying the central idea and experimental plan for each phase.
paragraphs.zh: 重构一份合理的获奖前研究计划。 我们利用奖项元数据、POR 和选定的论文，提示 GPT-5.1 扮演一位专业的 NSF 首席研究员。 关键在于，该提示将出版物视为受资助项目最终成果的下游证据，并要求模型推断出可能导致这些成果的合理获奖前研究计划，而不是对论文进行总结或复制。 模型被要求不提及重构过程，并采用我们生成的提案所使用的相同结构化格式：一份提案摘要、背景与意义，以及一个多阶段研究计划，其中需明确每个阶段的核心思想和实验方案。

sents.en: Reconstruct a plausible pre-award research plan.
sents.zh: 重构一份合理的获奖前研究计划。

sents.en: We prompt GPT-5.1 as an expert NSF PI using the award metadata, POR, and selected papers.
sents.zh: 我们利用奖项元数据、POR 和选定的论文，提示 GPT-5.1 扮演一位专业的 NSF 首席研究员。

sents.en: Crucially, the prompt treats publications as downstream evidence of what the funded project ultimately produced and asks the model to infer a plausible pre-award research plan that could have led to those outcomes, rather than summarize or copy the papers.
sents.zh: 关键在于，该提示将出版物视为受资助项目最终成果的下游证据，并要求模型推断出可能导致这些成果的合理获奖前研究计划，而不是对论文进行总结或复制。

sents.en: The model is instructed not to mention the reconstruction process and to produce the same structured format used by our generated proposals: a proposal summary, background and significance, and a multi-phase research plan specifying the central idea and experimental plan for each phase.

paragraphs.en: The resulting references should therefore be interpreted as plausible reconstructions of the funded research direction, not as recovered NSF proposals. We use them only as matched references for pairwise evaluation, providing a consistent comparison point grounded in projects that were funded and subsequently pursued.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，所得到的参考文献应被解释为对已获资助的研究方向的合理重构，而非恢复的 NSF 提案。 我们仅将它们用作成对评估的匹配参考文献，从而提供一个基于已获资助并随后得以开展的项目的一致比较基准。

sents.en: The resulting references should therefore be interpreted as plausible reconstructions of the funded research direction, not as recovered NSF proposals.
sents.zh: 因此，所得到的参考文献应被解释为对已获资助的研究方向的合理重构，而非恢复的 NSF 提案。

sents.en: We use them only as matched references for pairwise evaluation, providing a consistent comparison point grounded in projects that were funded and subsequently pursued.
sents.zh: 我们仅将它们用作成对评估的匹配参考文献，从而提供一个基于已获资助并随后得以开展的项目的一致比较基准。

paragraphs.en: The process-level reward evaluates the quality of the agent’s reasoning trajectory rather than only its final output. Each intermediate action (i.e., all actions before the final write ) is scored along two complementary dimensions: exploration and contribution . Both scores are produced by an LLM judge, mapped from the 1–5 integer scale to [ − 1 , 1 ] [-1,1] via the centering transform s ′ = ( s − 3 ) / 2 s^{\prime}=(s-3)/2 , and averaged equally into a per-action score. The overall process reward is the mean of all per-action scores; actions that were available but unused (i.e., the trajectory is shorter than the maximum allowed) are penalized with a score of − 1 -1 .
paragraphs.zh: 过程级奖励评估的是智能体推理轨迹的质量，而不仅仅是其最终输出。 每个中间动作（即最终写入之前的所有动作）都沿着两个互补的维度进行评分：探索性和贡献度。 这两个评分均由 LLM 裁判生成，通过中心化变换 s′=(s−3)/2 将 1–5 的整数尺度映射到 [−1,1]，然后等权平均得到每个动作的分数。 整体过程奖励是所有单个动作分数的平均值；那些可用但未使用的动作（即轨迹长度短于允许的最大值）会被处以 −1 的惩罚分数。

sents.en: The process-level reward evaluates the quality of the agent’s reasoning trajectory rather than only its final output.

sents.en: Each intermediate action (i.e., all actions before the final write ) is scored along two complementary dimensions: exploration and contribution .

sents.en: Both scores are produced by an LLM judge, mapped from the 1–5 integer scale to [ − 1 , 1 ] [-1,1] via the centering transform s ′ = ( s − 3 ) / 2 s^{\prime}=(s-3)/2 , and averaged equally into a per-action score.
sents.zh: 这两个评分均由 LLM 裁判生成，通过中心化变换 s′=(s−3)/2 将 1–5 的整数尺度映射到 [−1,1]，然后等权平均得到每个动作的分数。

sents.en: The overall process reward is the mean of all per-action scores; actions that were available but unused (i.e., the trajectory is shorter than the maximum allowed) are penalized with a score of − 1 -1 .
sents.zh: 整体过程奖励是所有单个动作分数的平均值；那些可用但未使用的动作（即轨迹长度短于允许的最大值）会被处以 −1 的惩罚分数。

paragraphs.en: The exploration dimension rewards actions that cover genuinely new ground relative to everything already explored in the trajectory. paragraphs.en: During training, we track two diagnostic metrics, action-level entropy and action-level similarity , that measure whether the model’s actual output behavior is consistent with its selected creativity level. Neither metric is used as a reward signal; they serve purely as interpretability probes.
paragraphs.zh: 在训练过程中，我们跟踪两个诊断指标：动作级熵和动作级相似性，用于衡量模型的实际输出行为是否与其选择的创造力水平一致。 这两个指标均不作为奖励信号使用；它们纯粹用作可解释性探针。

paragraphs.en: The core premise of our creativity-aligned framework is that selecting a higher creativity level should demonstrably change how the model acts, producing outputs with higher token entropy (more lexical variety) and outputs that are more distinct from the evolving proposal (higher divergence). If a model selects level 5 but generates outputs indistinguishable from level 1, the creativity selector is decorative rather than functional. These metrics operationalize that sanity check.
paragraphs.zh: 我们这一套与创造力对齐的框架的核心前提是：选择更高的创造力级别应当能明显改变模型的行为方式，从而生成具有更高词元熵值（即词汇多样性更高）且与不断演化的提案更具差异性的输出（即发散度更高）。 如果模型选择了第 5 级，但生成的输出与第 1 级的输出毫无区别，那么创造力选择器就只是装饰性的，而非功能性的。 这些指标将这一合理性检验具体化并付诸实践。

paragraphs.en: For each action, we collect the per-token log-probabilities from the model’s generation and compute the mean Shannon entropy across top- k k vocabulary candidates. This is averaged over all tokens in the action output to yield a single per-action entropy score. We then compute the Pearson correlation between the action’s selected creativity level (equivalently, its inverse noise level 1 − noise / max_level 1-\text{noise}/\text{max\_level} ) and this entropy value across all actions in a training batch. A positive correlation indicates that higher creativity levels lead to higher-entropy, more diverse token distributions.
paragraphs.zh: 对于每个动作，我们从模型的生成过程中收集每个词元的对数概率，并计算前 k 个词汇候选项的平均香农熵。 对此结果在所有动作输出中的每个词元上取平均，从而得到单个动作的熵值得分。 接着，我们计算动作所选创造力水平（等价于其反向噪声水平 1 − noise / max_level 1-\text{noise}/\text{max\_level}）与该熵值在所有训练批次中的动作上的皮尔逊相关性。 正相关表明，较高的创造力水平会导致熵更高、更多样化的词元分布。

A negative correlation (similarity decreases as creativity level increases) is desirable: higher creativity should yield actions that cover genuinely new territory rather than paraphrasing what has already been written.
paragraphs.zh: 对于每个动作，我们计算动作输出句子的嵌入向量与最新写入的方案草案（如果尚未存在草案，则使用问题陈述）的嵌入向量之间的余弦相似度。 我们再次计算整个批次中创造力水平与该相似度分数之间的皮尔逊相关系数。 负相关（即创造力水平越高，相似度越低）是理想的：更高的创造力应能产生覆盖真正新领域的动作，而不是对已有内容进行改写。

paragraphs.en: Training creativity-aligned agents requires substantial GPU compute. We mitigate this by working with an efficient 8B-parameter architecture, but scaling to larger models would amplify the footprint. Additionally, our reward pipeline relies on LLM judges (GPT-4.1 for feasibility/relevance during training, SciJudge-30B and GPT-5.1 for evaluation). Unlike similarity-based reward signals that compare generated text against existing corpora, we deliberately use LLM judges to assess genuinely new ideas—minimizing data leakage and preventing the model from learning to simply paraphrase known work from our dataset, which spans proposals as far back as 2018. This design choice comes at higher inference cost but is central to the validity of the precedence and originality signal.
paragraphs.zh: 训练与创造力对齐的智能体需要大量的 GPU 计算资源。 我们通过采用高效的 8B 参数架构来缓解这一问题，但扩展到更大模型会扩大其资源占用。 此外，我们的奖励流程依赖 LLM 评判者（训练期间使用 GPT-4.1 评估可行性和相关性，评估阶段则使用 SciJudge-30B 和 GPT-5.1）。 与将生成文本同现有语料库进行比较的相似性基奖励信号不同，我们特意使用 LLM 评判者来评估真正的新颖想法——从而最小化数据泄露，并防止模型仅学习如何从我们包含自 2018 年以来提案的数据集中改写已知成果。 这一设计选择虽然带来了更高的推理成本，但却是确保先例性和原创性信号有效性的关键。

paragraphs.en: Given the inherent complexity of our task, particularly the implicit objective of increasing the entropy of a model’s outputs, we have observed that training can become unstable, especially over longer training runs. High-entropy generation is at odds with the stability assumptions underlying standard RL algorithms designed for low-variance, verifiable reward settings. We hope future work will explore more robust RL algorithms that can handle the entropy increases required for creative reasoning. We also note that our infrastructure relies on Verl as the training backend and SGLang as the inference backend; their current joint support for structured, multi-step agentic frameworks is limited, and tighter integration would enable more scalable and reliable training pipelines.
paragraphs.zh: 鉴于我们任务的固有复杂性，尤其是提高模型输出熵这一隐含目标，我们发现训练过程可能会变得不稳定，尤其是在较长的训练过程中。 高熵生成与标准强化学习算法所依赖的稳定性假设相冲突，这些算法是为低方差、可验证的奖励场景而设计的。 我们希望未来的研究能够探索更稳健的强化学习算法，以应对创造性推理所需的熵增。 我们还注意到，我们的基础设施依赖 Verl 作为训练后端，以及 SGLang 作为推理后端；它们目前对结构化、多步骤智能体框架的联合支持有限，而更紧密的集成将有助于构建更具可扩展性和可靠性的训练流程。
